about.title: About JPG to PNG Notes
description: This page currently explains when JPG to PNG is a reasonable workflow and what it cannot do by itself.
Converting a JPG to PNG does not restore detail lost to earlier JPG compression, and it does not automatically create transparent backgrounds.
The interactive version is not part of the featured public surface until its implementation details, limitations, and policy wording are reviewed together.

howTo.title: How to Use This Review Note

steps.title: Check the source image
steps.description: Decide whether the JPG already contains visible compression artifacts or text edges that may make a different workflow more appropriate.

steps.title: Define the goal
steps.description: Confirm whether you actually need PNG for editing stability, graphics handling, or export requirements rather than assuming it will improve quality.

steps.title: Review the limitations
steps.description: Use the notes on this page to understand transparency limits, expected file-size tradeoffs, and when another destination format may be better.

steps.title: Verify the final output independently
steps.description: Before publishing or relying on a converted asset, confirm the output visually in the destination workflow.

tips: PNG is often useful as a later editing format, not as a magic quality upgrade.
If you need a transparent background, you still need a workflow that explicitly removes or masks the background.
For photo-heavy content where size matters most, JPG or WebP may remain the better target.

faq.q: Does JPG to PNG automatically improve image quality?
faq.a: No. It can prevent additional loss in later edits, but it does not recover detail already lost to JPG compression.

faq.q: Will converting to PNG create transparency?
faq.a: No. PNG supports transparency, but converting a JPG alone does not create transparent areas without an additional editing step.

faq.q: Why is this page not presented as a fully launched tool?
faq.a: The public site only promotes file workflows after implementation details, usage limits, and policy wording are reviewed together.

faq.q: When is PNG the better target?
faq.a: PNG is often better when you plan further editing, need sharper graphic edges, or want a more stable intermediate export for screenshots, diagrams, or text-heavy assets.
